## The kill — diagnosed, not guessed

First gate launch reached ~89% of 164 test files then exited `rc=143`
(SIGTERM), with **0 FAILED/ERROR lines** and no junit written.

Cause, from `journalctl`:

```
05:07:18 earlyoom[2703914]: mem avail: 12644 of 128804 MiB (9.82%), swap free: 0
05:07:18 earlyoom[2703914]: low memory! at or below SIGTERM limits: mem 10.00%
05:07:18 earlyoom[2703914]: sending SIGTERM to process 3568391 uid 1001 "pytest":
                            badness 980, VmRSS 2637 MiB
```

`earlyoom` runs as `-m 10 -s 10` with `--prefer (^|/)(pytest|python3?)$` and
`--avoid ...(claude|happy)...` — pytest is the DESIGNATED victim under memory
pressure on this shared VM. Our own process held only **2637 MiB**: we were
collateral, not the hog. Concurrently, a sibling session's Step 9c gate was
running `step9c_baseline.py compare --run-pristine` (pid 3633543, its own
`timeout 4200s`), which spawns a SECOND full pytest tree — two full suites plus
~15 live sessions on a 125 GiB box drove available memory to 9.8%.

Classification: `failure_class: infra`, shared-VM resource contention. NOT a
code defect and NOT a test failure — nothing in the diff is implicated. Per the
rerun discipline this was diagnosed before relaunch rather than blind-retried.

## Fix-engaged signals, declared before relaunch

1. **Serialize, don't race** — the relaunch wrapper waits for
   `step9c_baseline.py compare` to clear AND for `MemAvailable` > 40 GiB before

   self-bound).
2. **Shrink our badness** — `OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=4`,
   `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2`.
3. **Keep pytest temp off `/`** — `--basetemp=/mnt/eps-data/tmp/i2018-bt` (the
   data disk), plus `-p no:cacheprovider`.

Detached shape: `setsid /tmp/i2018-gate-run.sh`; breadcrumbs
`/tmp/i2018-gate.pid`, log `/tmp/i2018-step9c.log`, rc
`/tmp/i2018-step9c.rc`, junit `/tmp/i2018-step9c.xml`, launch record
`/tmp/i2018-gate-preflight.txt`. Survives this terminal closing; a successor

## Self-inflicted false DONE — corrected, recorded

The first relaunch appeared to fail identically (`rc=143` at the same 89%).
It had NOT run: the wrapper was still in its wait loop (`preflight.txt` absent,
wrapper pid alive) and the watcher had keyed its done-condition on BARE
EXISTENCE of `/tmp/i2018-step9c.rc`, which still held the FIRST run's file
(mtime 05:07:19). The `rm -f` of the stale sentinel sat AFTER the wait loop
inside the wrapper instead of before the watch was armed.

This is exactly the trap CLAUDE.md § Monitoring names — "never key a
Monitor/until-loop 'done' condition on bare file existence … remove any stale
sentinel at launch" (#779). Corrected: stale rc/log/junit/preflight deleted
BEFORE relaunch, and the watch now requires `preflight.txt` (written only after
the wait completes, immediately before pytest starts) AND `rc` together, so a
stale breadcrumb cannot satisfy it.
